title: Define and implement x-llm-req-parameter.validation.function
objective: Let request parameter schemas declare bespoke validation that JSON Schema cannot express, through x-llm-req-parameter.validation.function inline JavaScript functions that receive the parameter value and a read-only validation context, and run them in the shared completeRequest boundary before file materialization and provider use. Contract sections: requests/README.md#x-llm-req-parameter-metadata; requests/README.md#processing-order; requests/README.md#request-name-and-filesystem-safety; requests/README.md#evidence-boundary.

branch.name: WI-0023-request-parameter-validation
branch.rationale: Each work item is processed on its own branch.

request.text: Define and implement x-llm-req-parameter metadata for request parameter schemas so custom validation that is inexpressible via JSON Schema can be declared safely, documented in requests/README.md, tested provider-free, and integrated into the dynamic request work-item sequence. Operator clarification: we want to support x-llm-req-parameter.validation.function for an inline javascript function that has access to context sufficient to perform bespoke validation.

scope.name: metadata-contract
scope.description: Define x-llm-req-parameter.validation with a required inline JavaScript function expression and an optional failure message, its allowed schema positions, and fail-closed handling of malformed metadata.
scope.reason: Bespoke validation must be explicitly declared by each request schema.

scope.name: invocation-context
scope.description: Invoke each declared function with the parameter value and a frozen context exposing the parameter path, the complete resolved parameters, the schema node, request identity, working directory, and read-only filesystem helpers.
scope.reason: Bespoke validation needs enough context to check cross-field and filesystem conditions.

scope.name: result-semantics
scope.description: Define pass/fail return values, thrown-error handling, synchronous execution, a bounded timeout, and an isolated vm context without Node globals.
scope.reason: Validation outcomes must be deterministic and bounded.

scope.name: pipeline-integration
scope.description: Run validators through completeRequest after JSON Schema validation and before file materialization, substitution, and provider delegation, for CLI and library callers alike.
scope.reason: One shared boundary must own parameter validation.

scope.name: documentation-and-compatibility
scope.description: Document the feature and its trust boundary in requests/README.md, README.md, and SKILL.md, record the decision, and keep existing file-binding and summarize behavior green.
scope.reason: The request README is the authoritative llm req contract.

nonGoals.name: security-sandbox
nonGoals.description: Do not claim or build a security sandbox; request bundles are trusted configuration and the vm context only limits accidental access to Node globals.
nonGoals.reason: node:vm is not a security mechanism.

nonGoals.name: module-and-async-validators
nonGoals.description: Do not load validator modules or file paths, and do not support asynchronous validators, network access, or filesystem writes.
nonGoals.reason: Keep validation inline, synchronous, and bounded.

nonGoals.name: request-name-special-casing
nonGoals.description: Do not add validation behavior keyed on request names or change the summarize request assets.
nonGoals.reason: The feature must be generic and schema-declared.

nonGoals.name: provider-and-release
nonGoals.description: Do not make authenticated provider calls, publish, deploy, or claim production readiness.

items.name: metadata-contract
items.description: Parameter schemas can declare x-llm-req-parameter.validation with a function expression (string or array of lines) and optional message on the schema root, properties, and array items; malformed metadata fails before provider use.
items.reason: Validation must be explicit, schema-owned, and fail closed.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Valid metadata is accepted alone and together with file metadata on the same node.
Unknown members, non-string sources, syntax errors, non-function expressions, and unsupported schema positions fail boundedly with zero provider calls.

items.name: invocation-context
items.description: Each function receives the value and a frozen context with path, value, parameters, schema, request name and directory, working directory, and read-only filesystem helpers; array-item validators run per element and absent values are skipped.
items.reason: Bespoke validation needs sufficient, immutable context.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Context fields carry the documented values, are immutable, and run in deterministic declaration order with concrete element paths.
Filesystem helpers resolve from the working directory, are read-only, and bound text reads.

items.name: result-semantics
items.description: true or undefined passes; false fails with the declared or default message; a string fails with that message; a thrown error fails with its message; other results, thenables, and timeouts are bounded configuration errors.
items.reason: Outcomes must be deterministic and bounded.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every documented return form produces the documented outcome and failures stop before provider use.
Infinite loops time out, string code generation is disabled, and require/process are unavailable in the validator context.

items.name: pipeline-integration
items.description: completeRequest runs validators after JSON Schema validation and before file materialization, placeholder substitution, and provider delegation, for library callers and llm req alike.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Schema-invalid values never reach a validator and failing validators create no materialized files and make no provider calls.
llm req --p- assignments reach the same validators as library parameters.

items.name: documentation-and-compatibility
items.description: requests/README.md documents the metadata, context, results, ordering, timeout, and trust boundary; README.md and SKILL.md mention the feature; existing behavior and the full provider-free gate stay green.
items.reason: The contract must match behavior and the change must be additive.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Contract text matches the implemented shape and no longer states that validation is reserved or that request assets never execute JavaScript.
The full repository gate passes, including existing file-binding and summarize tests.
